speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Prime Minister in light of Singapore’s core inflation at 5.3% in September 2022 being at the highest since November 2008 (a) whether Singapore will consider tightening its monetary policy again; and (b) whether the Government will consider more targeted measures to rein in food and accommodation prices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: And it was among the earlier central banks in the world to do so, at a time when the pickup in global inflation was still quite modest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The effects of MAS' successive monetary policy moves are still working their way through the economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It will also take time for external- and domestic-induced price pressures to ease more discernibly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS will continue to deploy monetary policy as appropriate, to ensure medium-term price stability, while recognising near-term risks to economic growth from a slowing and uncertain global economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Member asked about whether the Government will consider more targeted measures to rein in food and accommodation prices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: On food, the Minister for Trade and Industry had, in October 2022, spoken about how (a) the appreciating Singapore dollar, (b) the diversification of Singapore's food supply sources and (c) Government assistance to lower-income and vulnerable Singaporeans should mitigate the effects of higher global food prices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As for accommodation prices, MND, HDB and MAS have, as Members know, taken steps to promote sustainable conditions in the property market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Government has also increased market subsidies to ensure that prices of new HDB flats remain affordable, as well as increased supply in both the public and private housing markets.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister of State clarify our exchange rate policy and how MAS manages monetary policy?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If monetary policy is tightened, would the Government ensure that the impact on unemployment in Singapore would not be adversely affected and how would MAS work with MOM on this?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Deputy Speaker, I thank the hon Member for his supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First of all, let me start with the second question.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are now undergoing a very dynamic, volatile and challenging global environment.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Employers must, on their own and also together with our partners in the tripartite arrangement, make their companies more productive, so that they can pay their employees more to cope with inflation.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Employers, employees and the Government work with tripartite partners to press on and we work together with all of these partners to transform our economy, to raise our productivity and also to turn all of the current challenges, which are not just faced by Singapore, but globally, into opportunities.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have launched 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These ITMs help to sharpen our competitiveness, for both our companies and our workers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They help to deepen skills and also set the stage for us to raise productivity.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: All this, in turn, will, hopefully, also help us to raise and to have more and better wages.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Government is helping employers by restructuring businesses and also upskilling employees.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have a couple of different schemes, including Workforce Singapore's Job Redesign and Reskilling programmes; Enterprise Singapore has the Enterprise Development Grant, as well as the Productivity Solutions Grant.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And on the whole, on the macroeconomic picture, our Economic Development Board is continuing to attract investments, even within this very volatile economic environment.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And the profile of investments has now shifted also to higher value-added, more innovative investments into Singapore and that will help to provide for, create more higher paying jobs, as well as good wage growth.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On the Member's first question about the fundamentals and the basics of our monetary policy, I thought it was useful to clarify to Members of this House, the market, general public, as well as students, MAS' unique approach to monetary policy, given that the Parliamentary Question (PQ) is also related to monetary policy.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is a very unique approach to monetary policy.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, MAS' exchange rate policy is Singapore's only form of monetary policy.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As Singapore's monetary policy is centred on the exchange rate and our capital markets are open, domestic interest rates are largely determined by global interest rates and foreign exchange rate market expectations of the Singapore dollar.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I thought it would be very useful for us to just clarify that MAS' unique approach to monetary policy is centred on the exchange rate monetary policy.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, one indicator of whether MAS has done enough to tighten policies is to look at money supply growth.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does the Minister of State happen to have data, figures about the money growth in Singapore's economy in 2020 to 2021, and what is the latest in 2022?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question, what is the impact of the accumulation of reserves by MAS over the last two years on the inflation picture?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does MAS or the Minister of State have any opinion or views to share on that?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does MAS or the Minister of State have any views to share on that?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Deputy Speaker, I thank the hon Member Mr Leong Mun Wai for his supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I invite him to file a separate PQ.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But I think MAS' monetary policy, as we mentioned, is very much exchange rate driven.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Right now, central banks all over the world have, by and large, also tightened monetary policy to combat inflation.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think what we are trying to do is also to make sure that, in a very dynamic environment, we monitor the rate of increase in terms of prices, as I mentioned in my reply.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But I invite the Member to file a separate PQ.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Since I was mentioned, I thought it would be useful to clarify with a follow-up question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Does MAS actually believe that its targeting of the exchange rate – which I understand, indeed, is the MAS' intermediate target; I teach that in my classes – does not actually have any influence on the short-term interest rate prevailing in the money markets?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I mentioned earlier on, MAS' monetary policy is focused on – in fact, it is our only approach towards monetary policy – our exchange rate-based policy.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will deploy monetary policy as appropriate and as the circumstances change.
